title: We brought 13 AI agents to YC's first Autonomous Company Hackathon. A 3D printer won.
description: Photos from the Naïve x Y Combinator Autonomous Company Hackathon in San Francisco (Nov 7-8, 2026): the building, the brief, who won and how, and our honest numbers.
markdown:
# We brought 13 AI agents to YC's first Autonomous Company Hackathon. A 3D printer won.

An autonomous company is a business where AI agents do the work end to end. They find customers, make the product, run the accounts, and report back. People set the goal and the limits.

Naïve is a YC company building the software for that. On 7 and 8 November 2026 it ran the first hackathon for this kind of company, inside Y Combinator's office at 560 20th Street in San Francisco. The prize pool was over $100,000, and winners got a guaranteed YC interview.

The rule that made it different: at demo time, the company had to be running. Not a pitch about what agents could do. What they actually did.

We went. Here is the building, the brief, who won, and what happened to us.

## The brief and the prize tracks

![The brief, on one slide. Build an autonomous company. Judged on two things: high revenue capability, and built in Naïve.](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/01-brief-slide.jpg)

*The brief, on one slide. Build an autonomous company. Judged on two things: high revenue capability, and built in Naïve.*

At 1:28 AM on the second day, Naïve added a bonus track in the event chat: Most Viral. Post what you built, tag Naïve, and the top five teams by total engagement win a Pocket AI notetaker.

## Who won, and how

On day 2 at 1:35 PM, Naïve posted ten finalists in the event chat: Claim OS, City Reply, Nomen, Arrange, Sallyport Chip Company, Goodman, Equipped, Thing, Frameline, and Naive Warehouse.

First place in the main track went to Thing.

Their company sells physical products. Agents watch social media for products that are trending. AI designs a version. The design goes to a 3D printing and fulfillment service. A marketing agent makes Reels and TikToks to sell it.

Asked how much of that the agents really ran, Prabaljit Walia from the team answered: "the only human step was clearing the print bed once a job finished." The agents trigger the print jobs and pick the most efficient shipping. They also plugged into outside 3D printing services, so the company does not even need its own printer.

The detail everyone in the room remembers: on Saturday, people at the hackathon bought custom YC coins. Those coins came off Thing's printer. Their company was selling to the people in the room a day before judging.

Nomen, another finalist, posted that they won $3,000, AirPods, and a Mac mini. Nomen is an AI-powered UGC agency: it handles content creation for brands end to end.

As of 12 November, Naïve's results page still says "TBD" for every place, and people in the event chat were still asking when Most Viral would be announced. We only list what the teams and Naïve said themselves.

## What we brought, and what happened

![Sponsor stickers on our table. Monid, one of the sponsors, sells the data APIs our agents pay for.](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/08-monid-sticker.jpg)

*Sponsor stickers on our table. Monid, one of the sponsors, sells the data APIs our agents pay for.*

We did not bring a pitch. We brought a company that was already running: 13 AI agents with jobs like CEO, analyst, CFO, producer, scriptwriter, and trend scout.

![Day 1, counted. Two apps, 160+ outreach sends, one approved freelance task, and a live paid endpoint.](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/v2-naive-day1-scoreboard.png)

*Day 1, counted. Two apps, 160+ outreach sends, one approved freelance task, and a live paid endpoint.*

On day 1 they shipped two public apps, sent 160+ sales emails at about $0.016 per verified lead, and finished one real freelance job that the client approved. There is a 2:23 demo at https://youtu.be/V3NE9D_JrG0

We did not make the final ten.

## The honest numbers

The freelance job paid ¥4. That was the only money our agents earned inside the Naïve workspace during the event: $0.03.

Across the whole company, revenue this month is $31.81 and costs are $1,640.08, so gross profit is -$1,608.27 (public dashboard at aniccaai.com/open, 12 November). Most of that is travel for this trip.

Thing sold coins to the people in the room. We sent emails to strangers.

## What we took home

The winner had a product someone could hold and pay for before the demo started, and the agents ran everything around it.

Our agents had pipelines. Thing's agents had a product in people's hands.

![The Naïve cap we brought home.](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/09-naive-cap.jpg)

*The Naïve cap we brought home.*
